english: The value of $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{45}\frac{1}{\cos 1^\circ+\cos\,(2k-1)^\circ}$ is equal to
solution: So the $k$-th term is $\dfrac{1}{2\cos k^\circ\cos(k-1)^\circ}=\dfrac{1}{2\sin 1^\circ}\cdot\dfrac{\sin\left(k^\circ-(k-1)^\circ\right)}{\cos k^\circ\cos(k-1)^\circ}=\dfrac{\tan k^\circ-\tan(k-1)^\circ}{2\sin 1^\circ}$
(Stopping the telescoping at $\tan 1^\circ$ instead of $\tan 0^\circ$ gives option (D).)
solution_full: Hence $\cos 1^\circ+\cos(2k-1)^\circ=2\cos k^\circ\cos(k-1)^\circ$. For $1\le k\le 45$ both cosines are positive, so no term is undefined.
Since $\tan A-\tan B=\dfrac{\sin(A-B)}{\cos A\cos B}$, with $A=k^\circ$, $B=(k-1)^\circ$ we get $\dfrac{1}{\cos k^\circ\cos(k-1)^\circ}=\dfrac{\tan k^\circ-\tan(k-1)^\circ}{\sin 1^\circ}$.
Adding for $k=1,2,\ldots,45$, all intermediate tangents cancel: $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{45}\left(\tan k^\circ-\tan(k-1)^\circ\right)=\tan 45^\circ-\tan 0^\circ=1$.

Check of the distractors: forgetting the factor $2$ gives (A); ending the telescoping at $\tan 1^\circ$ gives $\dfrac{1-\tan 1^\circ}{2\sin 1^\circ}=\dfrac12(\operatorname{cosec}1^\circ-\sec 1^\circ)$, option (D).
originality_note: New: the denominator is a SUM of cosines, cos 1 + cos(2k-1), which becomes the telescoping product 2 cos k cos(k-1) only after sum-to-product (way 5, the link is the discovery). Closest known: sum of 1/(cos k cos(k+1)) for k = 0..44 (published). Different because: the product is hidden; the student must first convert a sum into a product with the right pair of angles.
blueprint_concepts: Telescoping trigonometric series using tan/cot identities

concept_use.Sum-to-product and product-to-sum transf: cos 1 + cos(2k-1) = 2 cos k cos(k-1) turns each denominator into a product.
concept_use.Telescoping trigonometric series using t: 1/(cos k cos(k-1)) = (tan k - tan(k-1))/sin 1 makes the sum collapse to tan 45 - tan 0.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, function and interval is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath, is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Checked that no denominator vanishes for k = 1..45 and that the four options are numerically distinct (57.30, 28.64, 28.65, 28.15); (B) and (C) differ only in the 2nd decimal, which is intended as a cot/cosec trap. Changed: No change.
key_step: Recognising cos 1 + cos(2k-1) as 2 cos k cos(k-1), then the tan-difference telescoping.
justification: Two linked ideas (sum-to-product in reverse, then a telescoping tan identity) in single-correct format. Close to the telescoping of 2025-P2-Q15 (L4) but with options to check against, so one level lower.
